name.text: Angle between skew lines in a cuboid

questiontext.text:
In the cuboid ABCDEFGH, AB = {@ll@} cm, BC = {@ww@} cm and AE = {@hh@} cm. The lines {@L1@} and {@L2@} are skew.

[[input:ans2]] \(^\circ\) [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

Give lengths correct to 2 decimal places and angles correct to 1 decimal place. Keep full calculator accuracy until the final answer.

generalfeedback.text:
Slide one line, without turning it, until it meets the other. {@XP@} is parallel to {@L1@} and meets {@L2@} at {@PV@}, so the angle between {@L1@} and {@L2@} is angle {@nm@}.

Triangle {@XPY@} has a right angle at {@XX@}, with {@XY@} = {@vv2@} cm opposite angle {@nm@} and {@XP@} = {@uu@} cm next to it: \(\tan {@nm@} = \frac{{@vv2@}}{{@uu@}}\), so angle {@nm@} = \({@d1(th)@}^\circ\).

questiondescription.text:
Three-Dimensional Geometry: angle between skew lines in a cuboid

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.4: Name the angle equal to the angle between two skew lines of a cuboid, then calculate it in a right-angled face triangle.

Core

This question is adapted from Chapter 13, Section 2.5 (the angle between skew lines, found by translating one line) of School Mathematics Project, SMP Book 5 (Metric), ed. P. G. Bowie, Cambridge University Press, 1969: new skew pairs, cuboids and wording, randomised, with a naming step and named feedback.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

falsefeedback.text: Angle {@ans1@} is between {@oarm@} and {@L2@}. {@oarm@} is not parallel to {@L1@}, so this is not the angle between {@L1@} and {@L2@}. Slide {@L1@}, without turning it, until it meets {@L2@}: which line through an end of {@L2@} is parallel to {@L1@}?

truefeedback.text: That is the other acute angle of the right-angled triangle: you have the opposite and adjacent sides the wrong way round. For the angle you want, which edge is opposite it and which is next to it?
Your calculator is set to radians. Set it to degrees (DEG) and work out the angle again.
Your answer is close but not accurate to 1 decimal place. Keep full calculator accuracy until the end, then round the angle once.

falsefeedback.text:
[[if test="okr"]]

The tangent of your angle is {@d3(tn)@}. Slide {@L1@} until it meets {@L2@}: the angle is then in a right-angled triangle whose two shorter sides are edges of the cuboid, so its tangent is one of {@ll@}, {@ww@} and {@hh@} divided by another. Which two edges, and which is opposite the angle?

[[else]]

An angle between two lines, or between a line or plane and a plane, is between \(0^\circ\) and \(90^\circ\). Check your working and your calculator mode.

[[/if]]
